segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: Excuse me, I was told to come here for advice about, erm, Management Diploma courses?

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: You've certainly come to the right place. Hi, my name is Monica.

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: Nice to meet you. My name is Andrew, Andrew Harris.

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: So, Andrew, have you seen our diploma course prospectus yet?

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: Yes, I've already looked at it. In fact, I thought the information on course content was really useful, but I'm afraid I'm a bit confused by all the different

segments.speaker: WAYS YOU CAN DO THE COURSE
segments.en: full-time intensive, part-time and so on.

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: Well, Jet's see if I can help. I think each course type has its advantages and disadvantages, so it really depends on you - your own study habits, and your financial circumstances, of course. Are you working at the moment?

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: Yes. I've been working in the administration section of the local hospital for the last three years. And before that I worked in the office of a computer engineering company for two years. So, I've got about five years of relevant work experience. And what I'm hoping to focus on is Personnel Management.

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: I see. And are you planning to leave your current job to study, or are you thinking about just taking a year off?

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: I want to know what my options are, really. I don't want to quit my job or anything and my employers are keen for me to get some more qualifications but obviously, it would be better if I could do a course without taking too much time away from work.

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: Right, so you don't really want to do the full-time course, then?

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: No, not really. It's also a question of finances. You see, my office have agreed to pay the cast of the course itself, but I would have to take unpaid leave if want to study full-time and, well, I don't think I could afford to support myself with no salary for a whole year.

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: OK. Well, you have two other possibilities: you could either do the part-time course - that would be over two years and you wouldn't have to take any time off work - or you could do what we call a 'modular' course. You could do that in eighteen months if you wanted -or longer, it's quite flexible and it would be up to you.

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: Mmm. So what does the part-time course involve?

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: For that you would join an evening class and have a lecture twice a week. Then, you'd have to attend a seminar or discussion workshop one weekend a month.

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: What kind of coursework would I have to do?

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: Well, it's a mixture. You'd be expected to write an essay each month, which / counts towards your final assessment. You have a case study to do by the end of the course, which might involve doing a survey or something like that, and also you need to hand in a short report every four weeks. /

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: So, that's quite a Jot of work, then, on top of working every day. It sounds like a lot of studying - and really tiring.

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: Yes, you certainly wouldn't have much free time!

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: What about the 'modular' course? What would I have to do for that?

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: That's where you get the opportunity to study full-time for short periods. That way you can cover a lot of coursework and attend lectures and seminars during the day. And each module lasts for one term, say, about twelve weeks at a time. There are obvious advantages in this - the main one being that you can study in a much more intensive way, which suits some people much better.

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: And how many of these 'modules' would I have to do to get the diploma?

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: The current programme is two modules - and then you have to choose ~to work in more depth - but you can base that on your job, and so you don't need to be away from the office, and how long it takes is up to you. The important thing is that you don't have to study and work. You can focus on one thing at a time.

segments.speaker: ANDREW
segments.en: Yes, I can see that. It certainly sounds attractive! It would be more expensive, though. I mean, I'd have to support myself without pay for each module.

segments.speaker: MONICA
segments.en: That's true, so that might be a problem for you. Look, why don't you talk this over with your employers and ...
